title: Trade Unions Act, 1926 — Section 17 (Criminal conspiracy in trade disputes)

content.overview: Section 17 provides that an agreement between members of a registered trade union in furtherance of a trade dispute is not punishable as a criminal conspiracy if the agreement is only to do an act that is not itself an offence.
content.glance: Section 17 provides that an agreement between members of a registered trade union in furtherance of a trade dispute is not punishable as a criminal conspiracy if the agreement is only to do an act that is not itself an offence.
content.study: No office-bearer or member of a registered trade union shall be liable to punishment under section 120B(2) IPC / the corresponding criminal-conspiracy provision for an agreement in contemplation or furtherance of a trade dispute, where the agreement is to further an object of the union and the act agreed upon is not an offence.
